title: KV260 pl_clk0 probe — ROOT CAUSE of PS hang identified (clock mismatch)
context: Follow-up to Exp 661 (on-hardware PS hang) and the AXI simulation (results/kv260_axi_simulation_v2.json, which rejected the RTL-protocol hypothesis). This probe is READ-ONLY — it reads CRL_APB.PL0_REF_CTRL via /dev/mem mmap with no AXI access to the sampler. Does not risk wedging the board.

probe_method.access_path: /dev/mem mmap via sudo python3 (inline script via ssh)

baseline_k26_starter_kits_loaded.interpretation: k26-starter-kits is the default Kria app; uses pl_clk0 at 150 MHz.

post_xmutil_load_carnot_ising_v2_n64.interpretation: Our overlay requested 40 MHz (assigned-clock-rates = <40000000>) but Kria's fclk framework snapped to DIVISOR0=25 giving 60 MHz, not the closer DIVISOR0=37 (40.54 MHz) or 38 (39.47 MHz).

root_cause.name: pl_clk0 runs at 60 MHz, bitstream was synthesized for 40 MHz
root_cause.mechanism: Our N=64 MAX_DEGREE=16 bitstream was place-routed with timing-clean slack at 40 MHz (WNS +3.174 ns, 0 failing endpoints per results/kv260_bd_build_N64.json rebuild_40mhz section). At 40 MHz the critical path delay is approximately 10.312 + (10.312 - 3.174) = 22.23 ns. At 60 MHz the period is 16.67 ns — the 22.23 ns critical path EXCEEDS the period by 5.5 ns, violating setup timing on ~4,586 of 57,326 endpoints (same endpoints that failed in the 100 MHz attempt). Setup violations cause the AXI state-machine flops to latch metastable values on AWVALID/WVALID sampling. axi_bvalid never transitions to 1 because its input comes through a 22 ns combinational path that the 16.67 ns clock cannot resolve. PS master blocks forever on BVALID. AXI interconnect starves. PS goes unreachable, requiring power-cycle.

hypotheses_eliminated.hypothesis: RTL AXI-Lite protocol deadlock on split AW/W channels

hypotheses_eliminated.eliminated_by: this probe — CLKACT=1, clock is enabled and running

hypothesis_confirmed: pl_clk0 is running at ~60 MHz, not the 40 MHz target — setup violations in AXI state machine cause metastable latching and BVALID never asserts

fix_paths.name: Rebuild bitstream for 50 MHz (cleanly achievable from 1500 MHz IOPLL)
fix_paths.rationale: 1500 / 30 / 1 = 50 MHz exactly. Also 30 MHz (1500/50) or 25 MHz (1500/60) are clean. 50 MHz is the highest safely achievable without rounding.
fix_paths.procedure: Edit hardware/kv260/build_bd.tcl CONFIG.PSU__CRL_APB__PL0_REF_CTRL__FREQMHZ from {40} to {50}. Rebuild: source /tools/Xilinx/2025.2.1/Vivado/settings64.sh && vivado -mode batch -source hardware/kv260/build_bd.tcl. Expected wallclock: ~50 min.
fix_paths.risk: Low. Existing bitstream was timing-clean at 40 MHz with WNS +3.174 ns; a 50 MHz rebuild costs at most ~2 ns of slack, leaving ~1 ns positive — should still close. If it doesn't close, fall back to 30 MHz (1500/50) for guaranteed margin.
fix_paths.predicted_outcome: Bitstream closes at 50 MHz, xmutil loads with CLKACT=1 and DIVISOR0=30 (60/2 = 30), actual clock = 50 MHz, AXI works.

fix_paths.name: Force clock divisor via direct CRL_APB register write
fix_paths.rationale: fclk framework in kernel might honor a raw register write even when assigned-clock-rates didn't land precisely. DIVISOR0=37 gives ~40.54 MHz (closer to build target than 60).
fix_paths.procedure: On kria after xmutil loadapp, run: sudo python3 -c 'import mmap,os,struct; f=os.open("/dev/mem",os.O_RDWR|os.O_SYNC); m=mmap.mmap(f,0x1000,offset=0xFF5E0000); r=struct.unpack("<I",m[0xC0:0xC4])[0]; r=(r & ~0x3F00) | (37 << 8); m[0xC0:0xC4]=struct.pack("<I",r); m.close(); os.close(f)'
fix_paths.risk: Higher. Direct register writes bypass the clock framework; downstream drivers may assume a different rate. If fclk_cfg later re-runs (another loadapp), it'll overwrite. Not a durable fix.
fix_paths.predicted_outcome: Works for the immediate test but breaks on any subsequent loadapp.

retro_074_closure_gated_on: Successful AXI access after the 50 MHz rebuild + deploy + xmutil loadapp. This is a one-shot test; if the clock matches bitstream timing, the hang is resolved.
